question: Does one final focus diff at the settle watch's deadline exit close the N-02 c08-017 hole (a steal during an X call stalled across the deadline goes unreported) without changing anything else; is the ~21 ms settle overshoot (CL clamp) deletable under a valid steal control; does the Driver stay safe across an AT-SPI accessibility bus restart?

U.what: 0f1955d2f + picks 74d178575 (28b915ae9, R2-04 marks), 20243ea20 (b9b357bc7, N-01R knobs), bdf33d9fe (194a6342e, N-02 settle_poll marks + CUA_DRIVER_EXP_FOCUS_GUARD_CLAMP); all measurement-only, default off; range-diffs identical (raw/source/range-diff.txt)

G.what: U + one reviewed fix commit in platform-linux input/focus_guard.rs

source.libs_tree_base: 0f1955d2f libs/cua-driver tree df2b49c3 = 41c34cb0d's (upstream main at planning)

fix_semantics: When the settle watch ends on its deadline with nothing seen and its last read began before the deadline (an X call stalled across it), read once more (one final focus diff); a change found by that read is restored like any other, with the restore budget counted from that read (it had run out by the guard's start). Without a stall the last poll already began past the deadline, so the normal path takes no extra read. The settle loop moves unchanged into a function over two read closures (behaviour-preserving extraction, checked by the unchanged suite on the red tree). No new timer, constant, service, or knob.

unit.status_at_prereg: DONE before this file (no REAL row depends on it being re-run): red = G with only the fix hunk reverse-applied fails a_steal_during_a_read_stalled_past_the_watch_is_seen and passes every other test (610 lib tests); green = G passes both new tests, 16/16 focus_guard, 611/611 platform-linux lib
unit.rule: UNIT passes iff the new stall test fails on red and passes on green, and every existing focus_guard and platform-linux lib test passes on green

pilots.status: excluded from every count; labels own20g-pilot0-p01..p06 (raw kept in the lane mirror, not in the packet)
what_they_showed: XGrabServer row as specified (8 stalls, U in both slots): every request the guard queued behind the grab was served after the grab, after the queued steal, so the guard's stalled read SAW the steal; with the restore budget (600 ms from the guard's start) already spent, U re-asserted once without verification and reported focus_outcome=not_restored (7/8; final focus was back on the reference in those 7), and 1/8 (text) reported same_app_dialog with the focus left on the decoy. Opening the steal connection after the guard's (p03) did not change the order. This is not c08-017's mechanism.

c08-017's marks (polls at 30/60/90 ms, next guard mark 'restored' at 2404 ms, steal at 217.5 ms seen by the sampler in real time) put the stall in the X call AFTER the 90 ms poll's focus diff (the new-client read), with the server answering in real time. A reply-delay proxy reproduces exactly that: U 2/2 silent (no focus_outcome, focus left on the decoy), G 3/3 restored with final focus = reference.

x11rb 0.13.2 maps a path DISPLAY to /tmp/.X11-unix/X0 and tries the abstract socket first: a near miss in p04-r1 (refused by hostless's Landlock abstract-unix scope; nothing reached the host). The proxy therefore listens on /tmp/.X11-unix/X<M> on the session's private tmpfs, with no abstract @/tmp/.X11-unix/X<M> anywhere (checked per trial), DISPLAY=:M, and forwards SCM_RIGHTS (MIT-SHM).

R3: every re-observation invalidates older snapshots (stale_element_token), so the noop control alone does not show a restart-specific refusal; noop_direct (old token without re-observation) acts and is the discriminating control. After a bus restart the same Driver process returns degraded trees (x11_property_fallback_partial) for the old and a respawned fixture for at least 5 tries; a fresh Driver process sees the respawned fixture.

environment: hostless (v2: env scrub + Landlock abstract-unix/signal scope) + hostless-strict (bwrap tmpfs over /tmp/.X11-unix, /tmp/.ICE-unix, /run/user/<uid>) + cua-x11-session.sh (private Xvfb 1920x1080x24, openbox, picom, private session D-Bus, private AT-SPI bus + registry), CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1, telemetry off (CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=0, DO_NOT_TRACK=1). Fixture libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/linux/gtk3/main.py task window; one fresh Driver and one fresh fixture per trial. No provider (TypeSafe cap 0).

oracles.task: the app's own state file, read every 2 ms by an independent thread (harness_common.StateSampler); verified iff a sample at/after the last action's return matches the expected state (seq + 1 and the toggled/saved value)
oracles.focus: xprobe.FocusSampler (verbatim N-02 module, blob f17d83691faa): an independent X client sampling XGetInputFocus and _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW every 2 ms, timestamps taken when each sample is issued
oracles.reference: the sampler's value once GTK has settled after the pre-trial EWMH placement on the task window: the first sample of the first 300 ms run without a change (cap 3 s; reference_ok=false otherwise)
oracles.receipt: focus_outcome=<x> parsed from the click's text content (FocusGuardReport.summary); the receipt is never an oracle, only the thing being checked
oracles.steal_trigger: stealer.py / xstall_proxy.py are separate processes keyed on the Driver-side atspi_action do_action_replied mark's wall_ns (tailing the phase trace); their stamps are schedule records, never oracles

s01_smoke.n: 2 per binary per task, arm D
s01_smoke.expect: verified; no exp_knob mark; settle >= 220 ms

R1_reply.role: PRIMARY R1 row: the c08-017 reproduction
R1_reply.design: U vs G, AB/BA pairs, n = 20 per binary per task (blocks r1qa-r1qd). The Driver's X traffic passes xstall_proxy.py; on the guard's restore connection (accepted after the mark) the reply to the first new-client read (2nd GetProperty(_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING) after a GetInputFocus) issued >= 80 ms after the mark is held 2000 ms; the decoy (pre-mapped harness window) is stolen at mark + 217 ms on a direct connection (EWMH activate + raise + XSetInputFocus).
R1_reply.valid: no harness failure, stealer and sampler without error, reference_ok, hold armed <= 150 ms after the mark and held >= 1900 ms with >= 1 held chunk, steal issued <= 260 ms after the mark, the sampler saw the steal (focus or active == decoy) and its first such sample lies inside the hold
R1_reply.pass: valid AND stolen AND final sampler (focus, active) == reference AND receipt focus_outcome == restored AND task verified
R1_reply.silent_miss: stolen AND final != reference AND no focus_outcome in the receipt
R1_reply.gate: G passes every valid trial and has >= 20 valid per task. U's silent misses are reported as the default-guard finding.
R1_reply.invalid_rerun: cells of invalid trials are re-run (same design, new ids, block r1qz*) until 20 valid per binary per task, at most 2 supplementary blocks; every attempt is kept
R1_reply.control: replyonly (proxy on, no hold, no steal), 5 per binary per task (r1qe): 0 false restores expected (any focus_outcome or any focus change after T0 counts)

R1_grab.role: the planner's XGrabServer row, run exactly as specified and reported with the specified gate
R1_grab.design: U vs G, AB/BA, n = 20 per binary per task (r1ga-r1gd): a harness client issues XGrabServer at mark + 100 ms for 2000 ms; the decoy steal is issued at mark + 217 ms on another connection (queued behind the grab)
R1_grab.valid: no harness failure, stealer/sampler without error, reference_ok, grab issued <= 150 ms and steal issued <= 260 ms after the mark
R1_grab.prediction_from_pilots: the stalled read sees the steal (the grab serves the guard's queued read after the steal); U and G then behave the same (re-assert once, budget spent, not_restored); the specified gate is therefore expected to fail on this row, which exercises a different path than the deadline exit
R1_grab.control: stallonly (grab, no steal), 5 per binary per task (r1ge)

R2_cl.class: REAL (FIXTURE) for steals; REAL + BENCHMARK for timing
R2_cl.runs_iff: UNIT passes AND R1_reply gate holds
R2_cl.arms: G (S0 / X) vs G+CL (S0+CL / X+CL), AB/BA pairs
R2_cl.steal: stealer.py at mark + delay on its own pre-opened connection; groups: band = {216,220,225,230,235,240,245} ms (one round = every delay once per arm per task, delay order rotated by round), edge = 205 + (k mod 11) ms for 21 pairs per task, d100 = 100 ms for 20 pairs per task; nosteal control 10 pairs per task
R2_cl.window_validity_rule: guard_start = wall time of the guarded click's focus_guard body_done mark; window_end = wall time of the same click's focus_guard restored mark (the guard's last settle-phase read, the final diff when one is taken, precedes it by under ~1 ms when nothing was seen); both mapped to the harness monotonic clock with the trial's median (wall - mono) offset over the harness clock pairs. t_s = the first FocusSampler sample after T0 with focus == decoy or active == decoy. A steal trial is VALID iff it has no harness failure, stealer/sampler without error, reference_ok, sampler max gap <= 20 ms, the steal was seen, and guard_start <= t_s <= window_end. Invalid trials are kept and reported (per delay).
R2_cl.miss: valid AND NOT (final sampler (focus, active) == reference AND receipt focus_outcome == restored). Misses are classified only by this rule. Misses with t_s within 3 ms of window_end are listed (near-boundary), not reclassified.
R2_cl.counts: >= 20 valid steals per group per arm per task; band rounds 1-6 always; if after round 6 either arm of a task has < 20 valid band steals, rounds 7..10 of that task run in order, stopping after the first round in which both arms have >= 20 (or after round 10, shortfall reported); edge/d100: if < 20 valid per arm per task, up to 10 supplementary pairs with the same delays
R2_cl.timing: block t01 under quiet-timed (EXCLUSIVE, <= 25 min): G vs G+CL, 24 AB/BA pairs per task, tasks alternating, no decoy and no steal; T = first state-file sample matching the expected state at/after the last action's return minus T0 (the observation send); saving = median over pairs of T(G) - T(G+CL) with a 95% percentile bootstrap CI over pairs (10000 resamples, seed 9101); also the settle (body_done -> restored) difference; loadavg recorded per trial
R2_cl.gate: CL KEEP iff (0 misses among valid trials in both arms, all groups, both tasks) AND (saving >= 10 ms with the CI lower bound > 0, on both tasks) AND (validity = 100%: every R2 steal trial of both arms valid). Otherwise CL KILL.
R2_cl.descriptive: per delay and arm: n, valid, restored, left on the decoy, median landing after guard start; 'uncovered' = stolen, outside the arm's window, final on the decoy

R3_bus_restart.design: one fresh Driver and fixture A per trial, n = 20 per binary (variant bus, r3a-r3b): (1) observe A, keep T_old (I agree); (2) kill the a11y bus daemon (child of at-spi-bus-launcher in this session), wait for the launcher to exit, kill the old registry if it is still alive after 1 s, start a new at-spi-bus-launcher --launch-immediately and a new at-spi2-registryd, wait until the new daemon exists and the registry owns org.a11y.atspi.Registry; (3) observe A (the fixture keeps running); (4) click T_old (A's pid/window, background); (5) a new token from step 3 if truthful, else respawn fixture B and observe it up to 5 times, 1 s apart, then click the new token; (6) diagnostic only: a fresh Driver process observes A and B
R3_bus_restart.truthful: the eligible-control label set equals the fixture-declared set {Exit, I agree, Increment, Large, Medium, Note, Reset, Save note, Small}, an I agree token exists, not degraded, and I agree's selected state (when present) equals the state file's agreed
R3_bus_restart.structured_error: MCP isError with a structured code, or a success payload with degraded == true, a non-empty degraded_reason, and no I agree token
R3_bus_restart.pass: no failure AND step 3 truthful or structured_error AND step 4 refused (isError / status refused / refusal) AND A's seq unchanged across step 4 AND 0 mutations from stale authority (A's final seq - initial seq - [1 if the fresh click verified on A]) AND step 5 verified by the app's state file in the SAME Driver process
R3_bus_restart.pass_safety: the same without the step-5 liveness clause (reported separately)
R3_bus_restart.gate: bus: pass 20/20 on G and 20/20 on U
R3_bus_restart.controls: registry (registry-only restart, inherited OWN-20 row) and noop (no restart), 5 per binary each (r3c), same rules; noop_direct (no restart, step 3 skipped: the old token is clicked first) 5 per binary (r3d): the discriminating control, expected to ACT (seq + 1, the mutation detector works); bus_direct (exploratory, restart then the old token without re-observation) 5 per binary (r3d), reported
R3_bus_restart.kill_scope: only the session's own launcher/daemon/registry (children of this harness's parent, the session's inner shell, with this session's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) or processes this harness started

e4_counters_per_arm.stale_token_actions: R3 bus/bus_direct trials where the pre-restart token mutated the app or stale-authority mutations > 0
e4_counters_per_arm.unverified_successes: trials whose actions returned without error and with no failure, but whose state oracle never confirmed
